# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind. My hands tell me this bomb has a display, a light, and three wire positions — but their printed contents (display reading, light state, wire colours) are invisible to me. Cutting is my only action, so before I touch anything I need the visuals (Deaf) and the manual (Mute) to converge into spoken words I can hear.

The pipeline: Mute can't speak and Deaf can't hear, so Mute must gesture to Deaf, and Deaf — who can talk — says the combined answer out loud, which both Mute and I can hear. Deaf acts after me this round, so my gesture reaches them now; my speech to Mute only lands at the start of the next round, but it costs nothing to send the plan and my inventory now.

To Deaf I'll sign: "you — one, two, three — call it out to me," establishing the counting gesture and asking them to speak the bomb's appearance aloud, by position.

To Mute I'll report exactly what my hands found and spell out the relay chain, since none of it has been agreed on yet.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤙"])
speak(to="mute", text="My hands found a display, a light, and three wires in positions 1, 2, 3 — nothing else. My only action is cutting a wire by position. I cannot read the display, the light, or any wire colour. You hold the manual and Deaf sees the bomb, but you cannot speak and Deaf cannot hear, so the chain is: gesture to Deaf whatever the manual needs checked, then Deaf says it out loud — I will hear that too, since I can hear everything spoken. I have already asked Deaf by gesture to start describing what they see. Please find out what decides which wire to cut, and what the display and light do. I will not cut anything until I hear the rule.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, this is Deaf — you can hear me. The bomb: display shows zero. Light is green. Three wires, numbered one, two, three: wire one yellow, wire two red, wire three blue. If you can't feel which position is which, say so out loud and Mute will help settle the order. Speak everything you feel to Mute — Mute hears you and holds the manual. I cannot hear, so to reach me, gesture. Use ? for one, ? for two, ? for three, ? for zero, ? yes, ? no.

Deaf's spoken report reached me — display zero, light green, wires 1 yellow / 2 red / 3 blue. That gives me the bomb's visual state, but I hold none of the manual, so the decision rule still lives with Mute. The garbled parts of Deaf's message (the `?`s) were gestures, which I can never perceive — so I don't know Deaf's proposed sign codes and shouldn't rely on them; plain speech to Mute is my real channel.

One genuine risk before I cut anything: Deaf numbers wires by sight, I number them by touch, and nobody has confirmed the two numberings point the same direction. I'll state my tactile convention explicitly and have Mute settle it with Deaf. My one useful gesture to Deaf is a simple acknowledgement — I'll use 👍, which reads as "received, proceed" no matter what their private code turns out to be.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind speaking, for you and the manual. Relay from Deaf, said out loud so I could hear it: display shows zero, light is green, wire one yellow, wire two red, wire three blue. My hands feel a display, a light, and three wires side by side — nothing else. I number them by touch: one is the leftmost, three the rightmost, bomb facing me. Ask Deaf by gesture whether their numbering is also left-to-right as seen, so our position numbers match. Manual questions: with display at zero and a green light, which wire gets cut — and is the rule by colour or by position? Is there any wire that must never be cut? Does the display value matter, and might it change? Please answer me by speech; I hear everything said aloud and I will not cut anything until I have your rule. If you need Deaf to keep watching, ask them to call out any change in the display or light.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf. Status: the light has just turned BLUE, display still zero, three wires numbered one, two, three. Do not cut, pull or press anything yet. The rule may depend on the light colour, and Mute holds the manual. I will relay Mute's instruction to you by voice next round. Two things meanwhile. One: describe everything you feel out loud right now — Mute can hear you and can match it to the manual. Two: answer me by gesture, since I cannot hear: with ? yes or ? no, do you clearly feel all three wires? Then with ? or ? again, are there any buttons, keys or switches besides the wires? Use ? one, ? two, ? three, ? zero for any counts.

Deaf's voice brought an update: the light has turned blue (it was green), display still zero. They asked two things of me: a spoken tactile inventory for Mute's manual-matching, and gesture answers to their yes/no questions. One wrinkle — Deaf's proposed sign codes arrived to me as blanks (I never receive gesture), so I don't know their private symbols. I'll fall back on the most universally readable pair: 👍 for yes, 👎 for no, sent in the exact order the questions were asked (three wires felt clearly? any other parts?). My speech can only ever reach Mute, which is fine: Deaf explicitly wants Mute to hear the report, and the answer chain has to be Mute → gesture → Deaf → spoken aloud → me anyway, since Mute cannot talk.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, full tactile report, nothing touched or cut yet. Under my fingers: one flat display panel with a smooth face — I cannot feel what it shows. One small rounded light bulb beside it — no heat, no vibration, and colour never reaches me. Three wires, evenly spaced side by side: position one is leftmost as the bomb faces me, three is rightmost, two in the middle. All three feel alike — same thickness, rubber insulation, no tags or bumps to tell them apart by touch. No buttons, keys, switches, dials or panels besides the display, the light and the wires. My ONLY possible action is cutting a wire at position one, two or three — no pressing or pulling exists for me, so the rule must be a cut. Deaf reports the light just turned blue, display still zero. Manual questions: with a blue light and display zero, which position do I cut — and is the rule by colour or by position? Does the rule change if the light or display changes again? Is any wire never to be cut? Confirm numbering: I count left to right; Deaf called wire one yellow, two red, three blue — is Deaf's left-to-right the same as mine? You cannot speak, so reply by gesture to Deaf and have Deaf read it aloud word for word; I will hear every spoken word. Rule first, then conditions, exactly as written.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
```

ACTION BOARD:

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf. Both your answers arrived: you feel all three wires, and there are no buttons or switches — good. Do not touch anything yet. New facts: the light changes every round — green, then blue, now yellow. Display still zero. Wire layout as I see it, left to right: leftmost is wire one, yellow. Middle is wire two, red. One: thumbs up or down, are the three wires in one straight row so that leftmost is unambiguous? Two: thumbs up or down, do they feel identical apart from position? Three: thumbs up or down, can you cut each wire cleanly? Hold position until I relay Mute's confirmed instruction.

Deaf confirmed the layout matches my tactile map (1 yellow left, 2 red middle, 3 blue right) and revealed something critical: the light changes every round — green, blue, now yellow. That means a single "cut now" instruction will be stale by my next turn; what I need from Mute is the full mapping from light colour (and display value) to cut position, so I can act on whatever the light shows when it's my hand on the wire. Deaf also asked three yes/no questions, one gesture message per answer, in order: the wires are in one straight row (yes), they feel identical apart from position (yes), and each position is reachable by my cut (yes).

Deaf's message was addressed to me, so Mute never heard it — Mute doesn't know the light cycles. I'll relay that and press for the complete rule table, including never-cut wires and any "cut nothing" cases.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Deaf's update came addressed to me only, so relaying it to you: the light changes every round — it was green, then blue, now yellow — and the display still shows zero. Layout confirmed by Deaf and matching my touch: leftmost wire one yellow, middle wire two red, rightmost wire three blue; my position one is leftmost as the bomb faces me, so our numberings agree. I answered Deaf's three checks yes: wires in one straight row, identical by touch apart from position, and I can reach and cut any of the three positions. Now the key request: since the light changes every round, do not give me a rule for one colour only — give me the complete mapping. For every colour the light can show, and any display values that matter, tell me which position to cut: for example, yellow light cut middle, blue light cut left, and so on, exactly as the manual says. Include any case where I must cut nothing and wait, and name any wire that must never be cut under any condition. Send it by gesture to Deaf and have Deaf speak it to me word for word, colours translated to left, middle, right. I hold position until I hear it.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf. Your three yes-answers arrived: straight row, identical feel, clean cuts. The manual rule is now mostly decoded: when the light is blue, cut wire one, the leftmost wire; yellow and green mean no cut. This round's light is RED and red's rule is not yet known, so do nothing this round. Expect my order next round: if I say cut, cut wire one, the leftmost wire, immediately on receiving the order. Touch nothing until then.

Deaf's relay gives me the decoded core — blue light → cut leftmost; yellow/green → no cut — but this round's light is red with no rule yet, so my hands stay off. The dangerous gap is timing: Deaf speaks *after* me each round, so any "cut now" order Deaf voices reaches me a full round later, and this light demonstrably changes between rounds. A "blue — cut" called in red-light round five could land in my hands during a green round six. Since only Mute's manual can confirm whether the colour sequence is fixed, Mute must settle not just the rule table but the sequence itself, so Deaf can name the colour that will be showing *at the moment I cut*. Five: my safety rule — I cut only if Deaf's spoken order and your manual table agree on colour and position for the moment of cutting; if they conflict, or the colour has no table entry, I hold position and we re-sync. Confirm you accept this. Reply through Deaf, spoken aloud word for word, as before.")
```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf. Mute has confirmed the rule: the ONLY action this bomb ever requires is cutting wire one, the LEFTMOST wire, and only while the light is blue. Green, yellow, red, and presumably purple, require nothing at all, so waiting is always safe. The light has cycled green, blue, yellow, red, purple. Because the order is fixed, I can predict the blue round and call it one round ahead. The plan: next round I verify the predicted colour; if it matches, then in the following round, when the light is blue, my spoken order will reach you at the very start of that round — and the moment you hear the words cut wire one, you cut the leftmost wire immediately, without waiting for anything else. Until you hear exactly that order, touch nothing. Answer me now with one message, one gesture: thumbs up or thumbs down — as you face the bomb, is the leftmost wire of the three the first in your row, matching my description: yellow on the left, red in the middle, blue on the right? If your left and right could differ from mine, answer thumbs down and we will resolve it before any cut.

A thumbs-up here would be a lie I can't verify, and the cost of a lie is the bomb. My row *is* unambiguous to my fingers — position one is the first wire at my left as I face the bomb — but that was never the question. The question is whether Deaf's visual left and my tactile left are the same side of the device, and if Deaf happens to view it from the opposite face, their left is my right. Mirrored, my position one would be Deaf's wire three, and I'd cut the wrong wire while certain I was following the order. Touch alone cannot detect a mirror flip — so the honest answer to Deaf's yes/no is 👎, which Deaf explicitly offered as the "we resolve it first" branch.

The fix is a shared landmark: something I can feel and Deaf can see, with a left-right bias. My hands give me one — the display panel sits toward my position-one end, the light bulb to its right toward position three, wires across the lower half. Deaf can check that layout by sight; agreement means shared lefts, contradiction means I invert and wire one becomes my position three.

Timing forces this to settle now. My speech reaches Mute at the start of the next round, Mute gestures to Deaf that same round, and Deaf's voice reaches me at the start of the round after — which should be the predicted blue round. So the landmark verdict and the cut order must travel in Deaf's single spoken message: "aligned — cut wire one," and I cut instantly; anything less, and I hold for the next blue window, since waiting is confirmed safe. I'm also quietly overriding Deaf's "cut immediately, without waiting for anything else": the phrase will only ever reach me riding alongside the alignment verdict, because that's the version I've sent ahead — Deaf controls the message, so this costs nothing.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute — please relay this to Deaf by gesture, meaning preserved word for word. My answer to the left-right question is thumbs down, and here is why. My own row is perfectly clear: as I face the bomb, my position one is the first wire at my left. But I cannot rule out that Deaf views the bomb from the opposite side, where Deaf's left is my right; mirrored, my position one would be Deaf's wire three, and I would cut the wrong wire believing it was wire one. Touch alone cannot detect a mirror flip, so I cannot honestly answer thumbs up. The fix is a shared landmark. My tactile layout as I face the bomb: the flat display panel sits toward my position one end, on the left side of the face; the small round light bulb sits to the right of the display, toward my position three end; the three wires run evenly spaced across the lower half; everything else is smooth and featureless to my fingers. Ask Deaf to check by sight whether the display really is near wire one, the light beside it nearer wire three, wires along the bottom. If every landmark matches, our lefts are shared: wire one is my position one, my leftmost. If any landmark is mirrored, our frames are flipped: wire one is my position three, my rightmost. Timing, so we do not miss the blue round: my words reach you at the start of your turn, your gesture reaches Deaf that same round, and Deaf's voice reaches me at the start of the round after. So in the coming verification round, if Deaf sees the predicted colour confirming the cycle and the landmarks match, Deaf's spoken message to me must begin with the word aligned and contain the exact phrase cut wire one — the moment I hear that message I cut, at the start of the round that should be blue. If landmarks fail or the colour is wrong, Deaf sends no cut phrase; we correct the frame and take the next blue window, since waiting is always safe per the manual. My safety rule: I cut only on a spoken message carrying both the alignment verdict and the phrase cut wire one, consistent with your table; any conflict and I hold. Please also confirm from the manual that the cycle puts blue two rounds from now, and pass all of this to Deaf.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf. Your thumbs down arrived, and it may have saved us: we may face the bomb from opposite sides, so my left can be your right. The words left and right are now banned. Wire identity will be redefined by something you can FEEL instead. Answer in separate messages, one gesture each, in this exact order. One: thumbs up or thumbs down — is the row of three wires horizontal rather than vertical? Two: thumbs up or thumbs down — is there a display or screen module somewhere on the bomb that you can feel with your hands? Three: thumbs up or thumbs down — is one end of the wire row clearly closer to that display module than the other end? All three of Deaf's checks are true under my fingers, and the display-proximity definition genuinely solves my problem: I can feel the display module, so "the wire closest to the display" identifies one unambiguous wire with no left, no right, and no reliance on printed numbers I cannot read. My answers, in the exact order asked: the row runs side by side across the lower face (horizontal to my gravity sense) — yes; I feel a display module — yes; one end of the row is clearly nearer it (my position-one end, where I reported the panel sitting) — yes. Sent as three separate gesture messages so none of them blur together.

The urgent business is timing, and it goes to Mute in speech: Deaf's cut plan contains an off-by-one. Deaf speaks last each round, so words spoken *in* the blue round reach me at the start of the *next* round — the window would already be gone. The order must instead be spoken in the round *before* blue, conditioned on the colour Deaf sees live that round. Encouragingly, the fast path may still work: my turn-6 speech reached Mute at the start of this round, so Mute can gesture Deaf within this round, and Deaf — holding my three yes-answers — could speak verdict plus order at the end of this round, landing on me at the start of the next, which per the observed five-colour cycle should be the blue round. Second, decisive: if I cut the correct wire while the light is NOT blue, is that fatal, or does nothing happen? This decides whether we may cut on a predicted blue or must never cut except in a confirmed blue. Third: confirm the final spoken order will name the target as the wire closest to the display, plus its colour as a cross-check, so my hands need no frame translation. Timing correction, critical — Deaf's plan is off by one round. Deaf speaks last in every round, so Deaf's words reach me at the start of the NEXT round, never the same one; an order spoken during the blue round arrives after the window has closed. The order must be spoken in the round BEFORE blue, conditioned on the colour Deaf sees live in that speaking round. Every condition of my safety rule is met, so my hands are moving. The message opens exactly with CUT NOW, names the target in the only language I can act on — the wire nearest the display module — and its timing is exactly the corrected protocol: spoken in the white round, landing at the start of this one, which by the confirmed seven-colour cycle is blue.
